# ========================================================
# START OF FILE: sessions.py
# ========================================================

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Per-session records for every AI CLI on this machine.

`analyze_tokens.py` answers "how many tokens per account". This answers "which
session, how long, how heavy" — the per-session detail needed to rank anything.
It writes `sessions.json` into a machine folder; `stats.py` queries it.

Two dimensions are tracked separately and must not be conflated:

    cli       which tool you paid for   claude | copilot | codex | gemini
    provider  which vendor served it    anthropic | openai | deepseek | google

Copilot runs Claude models; that usage is Copilot spend, not Anthropic
subscription spend, so it is attributed to `cli=copilot, provider=anthropic`.
Filtering by cli answers "what did this subscription cost me"; filtering by
provider answers "whose model actually ran".

Every reader below had a trap that produces a plausible but wrong number, and
each one is documented at its reader. Verified against raw records, not assumed.

Usage:
    python3 sessions.py --out <machine-folder>
"""

import argparse
import datetime
import json
import functools
import os
import pathlib
import paths
import re
import stores
import sys
import urllib.parse
from collections import defaultdict

FIELDS = ("input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens",
          "cache_read_input_tokens", "output_tokens")

# Which counters are billed as sent to the model vs generated by it. Cache reads
# dominate every total by an order of magnitude, so a bare "tokens" number hides
# that ~99% of it is context being re-read rather than work being produced.
SENT_FIELDS = ("input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens")
RECEIVED_FIELDS = ("output_tokens",)

# Active time, not elapsed time. A resumed session's transcript can span days
# while holding minutes of actual work, so first-to-last timestamp measures
# calendar drift: it produced a "436 hour day" on this machine. Sum the gaps
# between consecutive turns and ignore any gap longer than the idle threshold,
# matching how Claude Code itself segments sessions.
MAX_ACTIVE_GAP_MIN = 15

# Providers whose models run on this machine. The tokens are real and counted
# like any others — a token is a token regardless of who pays for it — but no
# invoice exists, so they are marked unbilled rather than excluded.
#
# Three independent dimensions, and conflating any two produces a wrong number:
#   cli       which tool you paid for       claude | copilot | ollama | ...
#   provider  whose model actually ran      anthropic | google | meta | ...
#   billed    whether money changed hands   True | False
# Copilot running Claude is GitHub spend and Anthropic service. Ollama running
# llama is nobody's spend and Meta's model. Both are tokens.
LOCAL_PROVIDERS = {"ollama", "lmstudio", "local"}


def is_billed(cli, provider):
    """False when the model ran on this machine, so no invoice exists."""
    return not (cli in LOCAL_PROVIDERS or provider in LOCAL_PROVIDERS)


# ONE TABLE, IMPORTED. This file used to carry its own copy and it had drifted.
#
#     analyze_tokens.PROVIDER_PREFIXES   18 entries
#     sessions.PROVIDER_PREFIXES         17 entries, missing ("antigravity", ...)
#
# so provider_of("antigravity-1.5") returned "antigravity" from one scanner and
# "other" from the other, for the same session, in the same run. On this machine
# that is 26,927,559 tokens filed under two different vendors depending on which
# reader was asked, and BY-COMPANY.md is generated from one of them.
#
# Nothing announced the drift. The two scanners are cross-checked against each
# other on the TOTAL, which matched perfectly -- moving a session between vendor
# buckets does not change a grand total, so every consistency check passed over
# it. That is the fourth time this repository has shipped one rule as two
# copies: the flat glob in four files, the record/config test in one of two, the
# account fallback in three, and now this.
#
# Imported rather than re-declared. analyze_tokens does not import this module,
# so there is no cycle, and a fix to the table can no longer land in one place.
from analyze_tokens import PROVIDER_PREFIXES, provider_of      # noqa: E402,F401


def scanner_version():
    """A fingerprint of the code that produced these numbers.

    A content hash rather than a hand-bumped constant, because a constant only
    works if someone remembers to change it, and the failure is silent when they
    do not. Any edit to the counting logic changes this automatically.

    It exists because the consistency checks cannot catch version skew. They ask
    whether each slice sums to its whole, and a machine scanned with an older
    scanner is internally consistent and differently counted - every check
    passes while two folders quietly disagree about what a token is. Recording
    the version is the only thing that makes "these were counted the same way"
    checkable at all.
    """
    import hashlib
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    here = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent
    for name in ("sessions.py", "analyze_tokens.py"):
        f = here / name
        if f.is_file():
            h.update(f.read_bytes())
    return h.hexdigest()[:12]


def _machine_uuid(mdir=None):
    """The hardware_uuid for a machine folder, or None.

    Reads the UUID that update.py wrote into .machine-id, so every generated
    file agrees with the anchor check_consistency already uses. Falls back to
    install.hardware_uuid() when .machine-id does not exist yet (first scan,
    or a temp directory in tests).

    None is a legitimate return: a machine without a UUID is not an error, and
    nothing downstream must crash on it. check_consistency skips the UUID check
    for machines with no anchor.
    """
    if mdir is not None:
        mid = pathlib.Path(mdir) / ".machine-id"
        try:
            info = json.loads(mid.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            uuid = info.get("hardware_uuid")
            if uuid:
                return uuid
        except Exception:
            pass
    try:
        from install import hardware_uuid as _hw_uuid
        return _hw_uuid()
    except Exception:
        return None


def stamped(doc, mdir=None):
    """Stamp a document with the scanner version and hardware UUID.

    Every artifact, not just totals.json and sessions.json. Measured after the
    field was introduced: it reached 2 of the 5 machine-readable files, so
    hardware.json, lifetime.json and stats.json carried numbers that could not
    be traced to the code that produced them — and a number whose provenance is
    unknown is a number that cannot be compared to another machine's.

    That gap is exactly what the field was added to close. It was created three
    minutes after a scan silently lost 4,691,850,175 tokens, precisely so a
    figure could be tied to a scanner; leaving three of five files unstamped
    reopened the same hole in the files nobody thought to check.

    One helper rather than the same line copied into three writers: this
    codebase has shipped the same defect four separate times by duplicating a
    rule instead of sharing it.

    hardware_uuid is read from .machine-id (the anchor check_consistency.py
    checks against) and is None when the folder has not been claimed yet.
    """
    if isinstance(doc, dict):
        doc["scanner_version"] = scanner_version()
        uuid = _machine_uuid(mdir)
        if uuid:
            doc["hardware_uuid"] = uuid
    return doc


def blank():
    return dict.fromkeys(FIELDS, 0)


def total(t):
    return sum(t[k] for k in FIELDS)


def iso_to_dt(s):
    if not s:
        return None
    try:
        return datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except Exception:
        return None


def active_minutes(stamps, threshold=None):
    """Minutes of work: consecutive gaps, discarding idle stretches.

    The threshold is a judgement call and the result moves with it. Measured
    over 104,537 real inter-turn gaps on one machine:

        1 min -> 117.9 h      15 min -> 286.0 h      60 min -> 407.4 h

    So roughly 59% of the reported figure comes from gaps between 1 and 15
    minutes, which are genuinely ambiguous - reading output looks exactly like
    walking away. 15 is defensible because 96.4% of gaps are under 1 minute and
    the p99 is 4.1, so the threshold only adjudicates a thin tail. It is not
    "true" though, and `duration_tight_min` is recorded alongside it so the
    number can be read as the range it actually is rather than a point.

    What makes this bounded at all is having 104,537 intermediate events. An
    editor that records only a launch and a last write has two points and no
    threshold can rescue it, which is why editors report launches and not hours.
    """
    ts = sorted(t for t in (iso_to_dt(s) for s in stamps) if t)
    cap = MAX_ACTIVE_GAP_MIN if threshold is None else threshold
    mins = 0.0
    for a, b in zip(ts, ts[1:]):
        gap = (b - a).total_seconds() / 60
        if 0 < gap <= cap:
            mins += gap
    return round(mins, 1)


def finish(rec):
    """Derive duration and the sent/received split once a session is complete."""
    stamps = rec.pop("_stamps", [])
    rec["duration_min"] = active_minutes(stamps)
    # The same session under a 1-minute threshold: a hard floor on how much of
    # this is unambiguously work rather than a gap someone chose to call work.
    rec["duration_tight_min"] = active_minutes(stamps, 1)
    rec["elapsed_min"] = None
    a, b = iso_to_dt(rec.get("start")), iso_to_dt(rec.get("end"))
    if a and b and b >= a:
        rec["elapsed_min"] = round((b - a).total_seconds() / 60, 1)
    t = rec["tokens"]
    rec["total"] = total(t)
    rec["sent"] = sum(t[k] for k in SENT_FIELDS)
    rec["received"] = sum(t[k] for k in RECEIVED_FIELDS)
    models = rec.pop("_models", {})
    rec["model"] = max(models, key=models.get) if models else "unknown"
    rec["provider"] = provider_of(rec["model"])
    # Counted in every token total; excluded only where the question is spend.
    rec["billed"] = is_billed(rec.get("cli"), rec["provider"])
    return rec


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# claude — <config>/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl (+ nested subagents)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _claude_account(config_dir, home):
    """Which account a profile is signed into — analyze_tokens' rule, not a copy.

    This WAS a copy, and the copy is what made the sandbox profiles countable:
    `config_dir.name == ".claude"` sent any directory called `.claude` anywhere
    on the disk to read `home/.claude.json`, so ~/Desktop/standout_full/.claude
    reached the LIVE DEFAULT PROFILE's config and 489 M tokens were attributed
    to a real person on no evidence at all. The same three lines existed in
    analyze_tokens.account_for and again, differently, in read_claude_orphans.
    One rule now, in analyze_tokens.profile_claim / account_from.

    None means the profile claims no account, in which case it is not counted.
    """
    from analyze_tokens import account_for
    return account_for(config_dir, home)


# Where Claude Code token data does and does not live, so nobody re-searches
# these. Checked on 2026-08-04:
#
#   projects/**.jsonl   THE source. Complete, per-turn, all four counters.
#                       Deleted by the cleanup sweep after cleanupPeriodDays.
#   stats-cache.json    Lifetime per-model totals including cache. Survives the
#                       sweep — but is FROZEN, not live: ~/.claude stopped at
#                       2026-05-17 and ~/.claude-alt at 2026-07-11 despite being
#                       in daily use. A historical snapshot, not a running total.
#   history.jsonl       Live and never pruned, but carries NO token counts. Good
#                       for proving a session existed; useless for its cost.
#   sessions/*.json     Process bookkeeping only — pid, cwd, status, version.
#                       No token fields at all.
#   telemetry/          Failed-event payloads. Not usage.
#
# So there is no live counter that outlives the transcripts. The only durable
# record of a session's tokens is a scan taken while its transcript still
# exists, which is why these scans are committed.
#
# Also checked: `claude-skip` is a shell alias for
# `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`, not a config directory. Its sessions
# land in whichever profile is active, so nothing is missed by it.


# PERSISTENT COUNTERS: searched exhaustively, one exists. Recorded so these are
# not re-hunted, since each took real effort to rule out:
#
#   Claude Code   stats-cache.json — EXISTS. Lifetime per-model totals including
#                 cache, survives the cleanup sweep. FROZEN though: ~/.claude
#                 stopped 2026-05-17, ~/.claude-alt 2026-07-11 on a profile in
#                 daily use. Historical value only.
#   Gemini CLI    NONE. The code enumerates its own write surface in
#                 gemini-cli-core/dist/src/config/storage.js — 23 paths, not one
#                 a stats cache. Its metrics object is a private in-memory field
#                 re-initialised per process, and file telemetry only writes when
#                 telemetryOutfile is set, which it is not.
#   Antigravity   NONE at tool level. Every non-steps table enumerated; no token
#                 column in any of the 17 DBs. Usage exists only per-call, in the
#                 protobuf this file already decodes.
#   Copilot CLI   NONE. Usage exists only in session.shutdown rollups, so a
#                 session that crashed without one contributes nothing and always
#                 will. config.json has firstLaunchAt but no counters.
#   Ollama        NONE, and no per-session data either. ~/.ollama holds three
#                 files: two SSH keys and a shell history. Nothing anywhere
#                 records prompt_eval_count or eval_count.
#
# So Claude Code is the only tool that remembers its own usage after deleting
# the evidence, and even it stopped. For every other tool a scan taken while the
# session records still exist is the only durable record.


# Directories that hold copies of records rather than a tool's live storage, or
# that are too big to be worth walking. Skipped when searching for tool storage.
SKIP_DIRS = {"node_modules", ".git", "corpus", "merged", "deadreckon-record",
             "archive", "snap", ".cache", "venv", ".venv", "__pycache__",
             "site-packages", ".Trash", "Trash"}


def tool_roots(home, rels, max_depth=4):
    """Every directory on this machine holding one tool's session records.

    Each reader used to be a single hardcoded `home / ".<tool>/..."`. That is
    one guess at where a tool keeps its data, and silence when the guess is
    wrong — the failure that read Copilot as 0 on flat-layout machines, Gemini
    as 0 where it writes .jsonl, and every VS Code-hosted tool as "not
    installed" off Linux. The same shape was still in seven readers after those
    were fixed one at a time.

    So: look in the canonical place, honour the XDG overrides, and then walk the
    home directory to `max_depth` for a directory of the same name anywhere else
    — a second checkout, a copied profile, a staging tree. On the machine this
    was written on, four copied Claude profiles under ~/Desktop held 817,889,443
    tokens that existed in no live profile, because a copy resets mtime and the
    tool's own cleanup never reaches it.

    Returns real directories only, deduplicated by resolved path so a symlink
    and its target are not both walked.
    """
    seen, out = set(), []

    def add(p):
        try:
            key = p.resolve()
        except OSError:
            return
        if key in seen or not p.is_dir():
            return
        seen.add(key)
        out.append(p)

    rels = [r.replace("~/", "").lstrip("/") for r in rels]
    for rel in rels:
        add(home / rel)

    # THE TOOL'S OWN RELOCATION VARIABLE, which is a different thing from XDG
    # and moves more. $CODEX_HOME, $COPILOT_HOME, $GEMINI_CLI_HOME and
    # $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR each replace the whole dotdir, not a prefix of it, and
    # each can point outside the home directory entirely — at which point the
    # walk below cannot find it either, because the walk starts at home. So the
    # reader read zero, the store map resolved to [], and a tool in daily use
    # was reported identically to a tool nobody installed.
    #
    # stores.RELOCATIONS is the one definition; asking it here rather than
    # restating it is the whole reason stores.py exists.
    for rel in rels:
        for extra in stores.relocations(rel, str(home)):
            add(pathlib.Path(extra))

    for var, prefix in (("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", ".config"), ("XDG_DATA_HOME", ".local/share")):
        root = os.environ.get(var)
        if not root:
            continue
        for rel in rels:
            add(pathlib.Path(root).expanduser() / rel)
            if rel.startswith(prefix + "/"):        # ~/.config/X -> $XDG/X
                add(pathlib.Path(root).expanduser() / rel[len(prefix) + 1:])

    # The leading component is the tool's own directory name — that is what is
    # searched for elsewhere, with the rest of the path re-applied beneath it.
    wanted = {}
    for rel in rels:
        parts = rel.split("/")
        wanted.setdefault(parts[0], set()).add("/".join(parts[1:]))

    def walk(root, depth):
        if depth < 0:
            return
        try:
            kids = sorted(root.iterdir())
        except OSError:
            return
        for d in kids:
            if not d.is_dir() or d.is_symlink() or d.name in SKIP_DIRS:
                continue
            if d.name in wanted:
                for tail in wanted[d.name]:
                    add(d / tail if tail else d)
            walk(d, depth - 1)

    walk(home, max_depth)
    return out


def merge_session(dst, src):
    """Two observations of ONE session, merged to the union of what they saw.

    Per-field MAXIMUM on the counters, via analyze_tokens.max_into — the same
    rule read_claude applies to two writes of one message, asked here of two
    copies of one session. Not a sum: the copies overlap and summing them
    doubles. Not first-wins, which is what this used to do.

    Not max-of-the-sum either, which is the third rule this repository invented
    (read_claude_orphans) and the reason max_into is per FIELD: snapshot A
    {output:100, cache_read:0} against B {output:0, cache_read:150} makes B win
    wholesale under max-of-the-sum and the 100 is simply gone.

    Everything else follows the same shape — the earliest start, the latest end,
    the largest turn count and duration — and the model is taken from whichever
    copy saw more turns, because a truncated copy's vote is a worse vote.
    """
    from analyze_tokens import max_into
    if (src.get("turns") or 0) > (dst.get("turns") or 0):
        for k in ("model", "provider", "account", "project", "billed"):
            if k in src:
                dst[k] = src[k]
    max_into(dst["tokens"], src["tokens"])
    for k in ("turns", "duration_min", "duration_tight_min", "elapsed_min", "end"):
        a, b = dst.get(k), src.get(k)
        if b is not None and (a is None or b > a):
            dst[k] = b
    a, b = dst.get("start"), src.get("start")
    if b is not None and (a is None or b < a):
        dst["start"] = b
    for k, v in src.items():
        if dst.get(k) is None and v is not None:
            dst[k] = v
    t = dst["tokens"]
    dst["total"] = total(t)
    dst["sent"] = sum(t[k] for k in SENT_FIELDS)
    dst["received"] = sum(t[k] for k in RECEIVED_FIELDS)
    return dst


def multi_base(*rels, key="session_id"):
    """Run a reader against every location its tool's data was found in.

    The reader keeps its body and takes the base directory as an argument. This
    wrapper supplies each one in turn and merges the results.

    UNION WITH MAXIMUM, not first-wins. This used to be `if k in seen:
    continue`, so whichever location the walk reached first supplied the whole
    session and the rest of the record was thrown away. That is right for a pure
    copy and wrong for the copies that actually exist, because retention deleted
    the tail of one of them: driven against read_codex, a full 6-turn rollout
    plus a truncated copy of it gives 675 one way round and 110 the other — an
    83.7% loss decided by which directory the copy happens to sit in. A number
    that moves when nothing but the filesystem layout moves is not a
    measurement.

    `wrapper.rels` is published so a caller that has the SAME data somewhere
    else — the corpus, an archive — can work out which sub-path of that copy is
    this reader's base, instead of a hand-written second table. A hand-written
    table is how the counter and the corpus ended up covering different ground
    without either one saying so.
    """
    def deco(fn):
        @functools.wraps(fn)
        def wrapper(home, base=None):
            if base is not None:
                return fn(home, base)
            out, seen = [], {}
            for b in tool_roots(home, rels):
                for rec in fn(home, b) or []:
                    k = rec.get(key)
                    if k is None:
                        out.append(rec)
                        continue
                    if k in seen:
                        merge_session(seen[k], rec)
                        continue
                    seen[k] = rec
                    out.append(rec)
            return out
        wrapper.rels = rels
        return wrapper
    return deco


def _probe(p, blind, want="dir"):
    """is_dir()/is_file() that survives EACCES and NAMES what it could not read.

    pathlib suppresses ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EBADF and ELOOP and RE-RAISES EACCES.
    That is the correct default everywhere else and it is fatal here: `chmod
    000` on one profile took sessions.py down with

        PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied:
        '<home>/.claude/history.jsonl'

    out of read_history(), which main() calls OUTSIDE the per-reader
    try/except. The run then wrote no sessions.json at all while
    analyze_tokens.py exited 0 on the same tree, and check_consistency ran
    EIGHT FEWER CHECKS against the machine folder left holding totals.json
    alone — a crash that presents as a quieter, cleaner audit.

    `blind` is a required argument and there is no swallow-only path.
    Answering False and saying nothing would make an unreadable profile report
    identically to one that was never there, which is the bug this repository
    has now shipped seven times in four disguises.
    """
    try:
        return p.is_dir() if want == "dir" else p.is_file()
    except PermissionError:
        blind.append(str(p))
        return False
    except OSError:
        return False


def _jsonl_under(root, blind):
    """Every *.jsonl below `root`, plus the directories that would not open.

    `Path.rglob` and `Path.glob` swallow EACCES and yield nothing — there is no
    flag, no callback and no exception. `os.walk(onerror=...)` is the only walk
    in the standard library that hands the scandir failure back, which is why
    it is here and not the one-liner it replaced.
    """
    out = []
    def onerror(err):
        blind.append(str(getattr(err, "filename", None) or root))
    for dirpath, _dirnames, filenames in os.walk(str(root), onerror=onerror):
        for name in filenames:
            if name.endswith(".jsonl"):
                out.append(pathlib.Path(dirpath) / name)
    return out


def read_stats_cache(home):
    """Claude Code's own lifetime token counter, which outlives the transcripts.

    Each profile keeps stats-cache.json, and it is not a transcript, so the
    cleanup sweep does not touch it. It holds modelUsage.<model> with all four
    billed counters, accumulated since firstSessionDate — including sessions
    whose transcripts were deleted months ago.

    Measured on this machine, per profile:

        ~/.claude       cache 12,290,485,337   transcripts  5,547,678,789
        ~/.claude-alt   cache 11,440,918,343   transcripts  2,564,843,440

    Two fields that look contradictory and are not. dailyModelTokens is input +
    output ONLY, no cache, which is why it sums to 30,779,997 against
    modelUsage's 12,290,485,337 — a 399x gap that looks like corruption until
    you check: modelUsage's input+output alone is 30,779,997 exactly, matching
    to the token. Different units, not different answers.

    NOT merged into the transcript totals, and that is deliberate. The cache is
    lifetime-to-lastComputedDate while the transcripts are whatever survives, so
    the two overlap by an amount that cannot be determined — the per-day
    breakdown excludes cache reads, which are ~99% of the volume. Adding them
    would double-count; picking one would discard real usage the other holds.
    Both are reported, each labelled with what it covers.
    """
    F = ("inputTokens", "outputTokens", "cacheReadInputTokens",
         "cacheCreationInputTokens")
    out, blind = [], []
    read_stats_cache.unreadable = blind
    for cfg in sorted(home.glob(".*claude*")):
        f = cfg / "stats-cache.json"
        if not (_probe(cfg, blind) and _probe(f, blind, "file")):
            continue
        try:
            d = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"))
        except Exception:
            continue
        mu = d.get("modelUsage") or {}
        by_model = {m: sum(v.get(k, 0) or 0 for k in F) for m, v in mu.items()}
        out.append({
            "profile": cfg.name,
            "account": _claude_account(cfg, home),
            "total": sum(by_model.values()),
            "input_output_only": sum((v.get("inputTokens", 0) or 0)
                                     + (v.get("outputTokens", 0) or 0)
                                     for v in mu.values()),
            "by_model": by_model,
            "sessions": d.get("totalSessions"),
            "messages": d.get("totalMessages"),
            "first_session": (d.get("firstSessionDate") or "")[:10] or None,
            "last_computed": d.get("lastComputedDate"),
        })
    return out


def read_history(home):
    """The session ledger from each profile's history.jsonl.

    Transcripts are deleted; this is not. history.jsonl holds one record per
    prompt with a sessionId, a timestamp and a project, and it reaches months
    further back than the transcripts do — on this machine to 2026-01-14 where
    the oldest surviving transcript is 2026-05-05.

    It carries NO token counts, so it cannot recover what a lost session cost.
    What it does give is proof that the session existed, when, and in which
    project. That converts "we may have lost some data" into a number.

    Captured into the machine folder and committed, so the ledger accumulates
    permanently even as the transcripts behind it expire. This is the only part
    of the record that survives its own source.

    Prompt text is deliberately NOT stored. `display` and `pastedContents` hold
    what was typed, and a token counter has no business keeping that.
    """
    out, blind = [], []
    read_history.unreadable = blind
    for cfg in sorted(home.glob(".*claude*")):
        f = cfg / "history.jsonl"
        if not (_probe(cfg, blind) and _probe(f, blind, "file")):
            continue
        account = _claude_account(cfg, home)
        per = {}
        for line in f.open(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"):
            try:
                o = json.loads(line)
            except Exception:
                continue
            sid = o.get("sessionId")
            if not sid:
                continue
            ts = o.get("timestamp")
            day = None
            if isinstance(ts, (int, float)):
                try:
                    day = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(
                        ts / 1000 if ts > 1e11 else ts,
                        datetime.timezone.utc).date().isoformat()
                except Exception:
                    pass
            elif isinstance(ts, str):
                day = ts[:10]
            e = per.setdefault(sid, {"session_id": sid, "account": account,
                                     "profile": cfg.name, "project": o.get("project"),
                                     "first_day": day, "last_day": day, "prompts": 0})
            e["prompts"] += 1
            if day:
                if not e["first_day"] or day < e["first_day"]:
                    e["first_day"] = day
                if not e["last_day"] or day > e["last_day"]:
                    e["last_day"] = day
        out.extend(per.values())
    return out


def read_claude(home):
    """Claude Code sessions.

    Trap: a turn can appear twice — resuming rewrites earlier turns into the new
    file, and a subagent's turns are inlined into its parent as sidechain
    records. Both copies carry the same message uuid, so dedupe on it or the
    total inflates. Subagent and workflow transcripts are separate API
    conversations and DO count; a flat glob over projects/*/*.jsonl misses them.
    """
    out = []
    # The SAME discovery analyze_tokens uses, imported rather than repeated.
    # This function kept its own `home.glob(".*claude*")` after every other
    # reader had been widened, so the two scanners disagreed about which
    # profiles exist: 11,407,255,540 against 10,415,507,939 on one machine,
    # 991,747,601 apart, which is the four profiles under ~/Desktop that a home
    # glob cannot see. check_consistency caught it — "analyze_tokens ==
    # sessions" exists for exactly this, two implementations of one question.
    from analyze_tokens import find_config_dirs, MessageMax
    # One collator for the WHOLE machine, and one record per session id no
    # matter which profile it was found in. Widening discovery without this
    # counted the four copied profiles as extra work: 765 sessions and
    # 37,196,921,021 tokens against analyze_tokens' 11,414,194,297 — the same
    # conversations, four times. A per-record map cannot see across profiles,
    # so the copies each looked new.
    #
    # THE SAME OBJECT analyze_tokens.scan uses. There were two implementations
    # of this rule and they disagreed by 37,175 tokens on a single message.
    mm = MessageMax()
    per = {}
    # Profiles found and deliberately not counted, kept with their paths so
    # main() can publish them. A list, set on every call: `None` here means
    # read_claude has not run, which is not the same as "nothing was excluded".
    excluded = []
    # DIRECTORIES THAT ARE THERE AND WILL NOT OPEN. rglob swallows EACCES and
    # yields nothing, so an unreadable project directory inside a perfectly
    # readable profile subtracted 1,251,500 tokens from the fixture and every
    # partition still summed to its whole — thirty consistency checks, byte for
    # byte identical against the same tree with that directory left readable
    # and EMPTY. Walked with os.walk(onerror=...) because that is the only one
    # of the three walks in the standard library that will tell you.
    blind = []
    read_claude.unreadable = blind
    for cfg in find_config_dirs(home, excluded=excluded):
        account = _claude_account(cfg, home)
        root = cfg / "projects"
        try:
            projs = sorted(p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir())
        except PermissionError:
            blind.append(str(root))
            projs = []
        except OSError:
            projs = []
        for proj in projs:
            for f in sorted(_jsonl_under(proj, blind)):
                for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"):
                    if '"usage"' not in line:
                        continue
                    try:
                        o = json.loads(line)
                    except Exception:
                        continue          # truncated final line in a live session
                    msg = o.get("message") or {}
                    usage = msg.get("usage")
                    if not isinstance(usage, dict):
                        continue
                    sid = o.get("sessionId") or f.stem
                    rec = per.get(sid)
                    if rec is None:
                        rec = per[sid] = {
                            "cli": "claude", "session_id": sid, "account": account,
                            "project": proj.name, "start": None, "end": None,
                            "turns": 0, "tokens": blank(), "_models": defaultdict(int),
                            "_seen": set(), "_stamps": [],
                        }
                    # Dedup on message.id, crediting a running MAXIMUM — the
                    # rule itself lives in analyze_tokens.MessageMax and this
                    # reader runs that object rather than a second copy of it.
                    #
                    # Fixing only one scanner made them disagree, which the
                    # cross-check caught immediately:
                    #
                    #   FAIL analyze_tokens == sessions on HP Laptop Linux
                    #        14,619,003,145 != 6,608,178,238
                    #
                    # Measured on ~/.claude-alt: 33,790 rows, 33,790 distinct row
                    # uuids — a row-uuid dedup removed NOTHING — against 13,819
                    # real messages. Claude Code rewrites one message many times
                    # while streaming, each write a new row uuid with the same
                    # message.id.
                    model = msg.get("model") or "unknown"
                    ts = o.get("timestamp")
                    if ts:
                        rec["_stamps"].append(ts)
                        if rec["start"] is None or ts < rec["start"]:
                            rec["start"] = ts
                        if rec["end"] is None or ts > rec["end"]:
                            rec["end"] = ts
                    key = mm.key(f, msg.get("id"), o.get("uuid"),
                                 (sid, ts or "", model), usage)
                    # A turn is counted only when the message is new: a rewrite
                    # is the same turn, and so is the copy of it that a second
                    # profile holds.
                    delta, _meta, new = mm.credit(key, usage)
                    if new:
                        rec["turns"] += 1
                        rec["_models"][model] += 1
                    for k in FIELDS:
                        rec["tokens"][k] += delta[k]
    # Emitted once, after every profile has been read — `per` is keyed by
    # session id across all of them, so a session found in a live profile and
    # again in a copy is one record holding the union of both.
    for rec in per.values():
        rec.pop("_seen", None)
        out.append(finish(rec))
    read_claude.excluded = excluded
    return out


# Filled in by read_claude on every call; None until it has run once, so
# "never scanned" cannot be read as "nothing was excluded".
read_claude.excluded = None
# Same idiom, same reason: a reader that could not enter a directory has to
# be able to say so before it is ever called, or `None` and `[]` become the
# question instead of the answer.
read_history.unreadable = None
read_stats_cache.unreadable = None
read_claude.unreadable = None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# copilot — ~/.copilot/session-state/<session>/events.jsonl
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

@multi_base(".copilot/session-state")
def read_copilot(home, base):
    """GitHub Copilot CLI sessions.

    Trap: several record types carry token-shaped fields and only one is usage.
    `session.shutdown` holds the authoritative per-model totals under
    modelMetrics.<model>.usage.*. The others are context-window bookkeeping —
    session.truncation (tokenLimit, preTruncationTokensInMessages,
    tokensRemovedDuringTruncation), and the currentTokens / conversationTokens /
    systemTokens snapshots. Measured on this machine: 292,157,006 real against
    555,396,004 of bookkeeping, so a naive sum reports 848,753,178 — 2.9x the
    truth. assistant.message.outputTokens is a per-message fragment already
    included in the shutdown rollup, so counting it too would double-count.

    Two things the first version of this reader dropped, both real usage:
    `usage.reasoningTokens` (335,250 here) and the compaction pass, which is a
    genuine billed model call — `session.compaction_complete` carries
    compactionTokensUsed in two schema generations that never appear in the same
    event (13 old, 5 new, 0 overlapping), so both are read and summed.

    Only known token keys are taken from that object. It also carries `duration`,
    which is MILLISECONDS — summing every integer inside a dict named
    "...TokensUsed" adds 194,163 phantom tokens, and is exactly the class of
    mistake this file exists to prevent.

    Copilot runs both vendors (gpt-5.5 and claude-*), which is why cli and
    provider are tracked separately.
    """
    if not base.is_dir():
        return []
    # Compaction token keys across both schema generations -> our field names.
    COMPACT = {"inputTokens": "input_tokens", "input": "input_tokens",
               "outputTokens": "output_tokens", "output": "output_tokens",
               "cacheReadTokens": "cache_read_input_tokens",
               "cachedInput": "cache_read_input_tokens",
               "cacheWriteTokens": "cache_creation_input_tokens"}
    # THE SESSION ID COMES OUT OF THE EVENTS, NOT OUT OF A DIRECTORY NAME.
    #
    # Copilot has written two layouts. Newer builds use <uuid>/events.jsonl;
    # older ones drop <session-uuid>.jsonl straight into session-state/. The
    # first version of this reader iterated directories only, so on a machine
    # using the flat layout it found the directory, reported zero, and looked
    # exactly like a machine where Copilot had never been run. Grouping on
    # `rel.parts[0]` fixed that and introduced a worse one: the id became
    # whatever the first path component happened to be, so a base one level
    # higher than the reader expects — an archive that keeps the whole
    # `session-state/` folder — turned EVERY session into one record called
    # "session-state". Measured against the real archive: 32 sessions and
    # 591,663,934 tokens beside the live base's 31 and 295,831,967. Exactly
    # 2.00x, and one of the sessions never existed.
    #
    # `session.start` carries data.sessionId. Checked on all 261 real files
    # here: every one carries it and every one agrees with the file name, so
    # reading it changes no number on this machine and removes the dependence
    # on where the tree is rooted. The path stays as a FALLBACK for a session
    # whose start event is missing, and `session_id_source` records which of
    # the two supplied the id, because an id read from a directory name is a
    # guess and must not look like a fact.
    per = {}
    for f in sorted(base.rglob("*.jsonl")):
        rel = f.relative_to(base)
        path_sid = (rel.parts[0][:-6]
                    if len(rel.parts) == 1 and rel.parts[0].endswith(".jsonl")
                    else rel.parts[0])
        ev_sid = None
        stamps, by_model = [], defaultdict(blank)
        models, turns = defaultdict(int), 0
        for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"):
            if '"timestamp"' not in line:
                continue
            try:
                o = json.loads(line)
            except Exception:
                continue
            ts, typ = o.get("timestamp"), o.get("type")
            if ts:
                stamps.append(ts)
            d = o.get("data") or {}
            if not isinstance(d, dict):
                d = {}
            if ev_sid is None and d.get("sessionId"):
                ev_sid = d["sessionId"]
            if typ == "assistant.message":
                turns += 1
                models[d.get("model") or "unknown"] += 1
            elif typ == "session.shutdown":
                for model, m in (d.get("modelMetrics") or {}).items():
                    u = (m or {}).get("usage") or {}
                    tgt = by_model[model]
                    tgt["input_tokens"] += u.get("inputTokens", 0) or 0
                    tgt["output_tokens"] += (u.get("outputTokens", 0) or 0)
                    # Reasoning tokens are generated and billed, and sit
                    # alongside outputTokens rather than inside it.
                    tgt["output_tokens"] += u.get("reasoningTokens", 0) or 0
                    tgt["cache_read_input_tokens"] += u.get("cacheReadTokens", 0) or 0
                    tgt["cache_creation_input_tokens"] += u.get("cacheWriteTokens", 0) or 0
            elif typ == "session.compaction_complete":
                tgt = by_model["compaction"]
                for k, v in (d.get("compactionTokensUsed") or {}).items():
                    if k in COMPACT and isinstance(v, int):
                        tgt[COMPACT[k]] += v
        if not by_model:
            continue                      # session never shut down cleanly: no usage recorded
        sid = ev_sid or path_sid
        rec = per.get(sid)
        if rec is None:
            rec = per[sid] = {
                "cli": "copilot", "session_id": sid,
                "session_id_source": "events" if ev_sid else "path",
                "account": "copilot (local)", "project": "-", "start": None,
                "end": None, "turns": 0, "tokens": blank(),
                "_models": defaultdict(int), "_stamps": []}
        elif ev_sid:
            rec["session_id_source"] = "events"
        rec["_stamps"].extend(stamps)
        for ts in stamps:
            if rec["start"] is None or ts < rec["start"]:
                rec["start"] = ts
            if rec["end"] is None or ts > rec["end"]:
                rec["end"] = ts
        rec["turns"] += turns
        for model, n in models.items():
            rec["_models"][model] += n
        for model, t in by_model.items():
            for k in FIELDS:
                rec["tokens"][k] += t[k]
            if model != "compaction":     # a bucket, not a model — must not win the vote
                rec["_models"][model] += 1
    return [finish(rec) for rec in per.values()]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# codex — ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

@multi_base(".codex/sessions")
def read_codex(home, base):
    """OpenAI Codex CLI sessions.

    Three separate traps here, each verified against the raw records rather than
    assumed, and each one produces a plausible wrong number on its own:

    1. CUMULATIVE. Every token_count event carries both `total_token_usage` (a
       running total for the session) and `last_token_usage` (that turn). Summing
       the former compounds: 59,193,380 against a true 1,453,618, 40.7x.

    2. REPEATED. `last_token_usage` is emitted TWICE per turn — the repeat is
       byte-identical and always immediately follows the first. 60 of this
       machine's 122 usage events are such repeats, so even summing the right
       field double-counts: 2,859,773 against 1,453,618, 1.97x. Only consecutive
       identical payloads are dropped; two turns that genuinely bill the same
       amount are not adjacent in the stream, and the ground truth below proves
       nothing real is lost.

    3. SUBSETS. `cached_input_tokens` is part of `input_tokens`, not a separate
       bucket (244/244 records satisfy cached <= input), and
       `reasoning_output_tokens` is likewise part of `output_tokens`. The four
       stored fields are disjoint by definition, so the cached portion is moved
       out of input rather than added on top — the split stays visible and the
       total stays right. Adding it instead inflated this machine by 2,514,176.

    Ground truth for all three: each session's FINAL total_token_usage. After
    these fixes the per-turn sum reproduces it exactly, 1,453,618 either way.
    """
    if not base.is_dir():
        return []
    out = []
    for f in sorted(base.rglob("rollout-*.jsonl")):
        rec = {"cli": "codex", "session_id": f.stem.replace("rollout-", ""),
               "account": "codex (local)", "project": "-", "start": None,
               "end": None, "turns": 0, "tokens": blank(),
               "_models": defaultdict(int), "_stamps": []}
        prev_usage = None
        for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"):
            try:
                o = json.loads(line)
            except Exception:
                continue
            ts = o.get("timestamp")
            if ts:
                rec["_stamps"].append(ts)
                if rec["start"] is None or ts < rec["start"]:
                    rec["start"] = ts
                if rec["end"] is None or ts > rec["end"]:
                    rec["end"] = ts
            p = o.get("payload") or {}
            if o.get("type") == "turn_context":
                m = p.get("model") or (p.get("turn_context") or {}).get("model")
                if m:
                    rec["_models"][m] += 1
            if p.get("type") != "token_count":
                continue
            last = ((p.get("info") or {}).get("last_token_usage")) or {}
            if not last:
                continue
            key = json.dumps(last, sort_keys=True)
            if key == prev_usage:
                continue                  # trap 2: the re-emission of this turn
            prev_usage = key
            rec["turns"] += 1
            inp = last.get("input_tokens", 0) or 0
            cached = last.get("cached_input_tokens", 0) or 0
            rec["tokens"]["input_tokens"] += max(0, inp - cached)
            rec["tokens"]["cache_read_input_tokens"] += min(cached, inp)
            rec["tokens"]["output_tokens"] += last.get("output_tokens", 0) or 0
        if rec["turns"]:
            if not rec["_models"]:
                rec["_models"]["codex"] += 1
            out.append(finish(rec))
    return out


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# gemini — ~/.gemini/tmp/<projectHash>/chats/session-<ts>-<id>.json
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _gemini_docs(f):
    """Session documents from a Gemini chat file, whichever way it is written.

    A whole-file JSON object, or JSON Lines where each line may be a full
    session or a single message. Anything unparseable is skipped rather than
    aborting the file — one truncated line in a live session must not cost the
    whole conversation.
    """
    try:
        text = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
    except Exception:
        return
    try:
        d = json.loads(text)
        yield d if isinstance(d, dict) else {"messages": d}
        return
    except Exception:
        pass
    loose = []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        try:
            o = json.loads(line)
        except Exception:
            continue
        if isinstance(o, dict) and isinstance(o.get("messages"), list):
            yield o
        elif isinstance(o, dict):
            loose.append(o)          # a bare message record
    if loose:
        yield {"messages": loose}


@multi_base(".gemini/tmp")
def read_gemini(home, base):
    """Google Gemini CLI sessions.

    This reader exists because the previous version of this repo declared Gemini
    uncountable. That was wrong by 1,468,362,549 tokens — the single largest
    error the project has made. The claim rested on grepping ~/.gemini for
    "token" and finding mostly anyio's CapacityLimiter.total_tokens (concurrency
    slots) in 27 vendored library files, then stopping. The real usage was in a
    directory that grep never reached, recorded under the Gemini API's own field
    names.

    Two traps, both confirmed across all 4,559 usage records here:

    - `cached` (cachedContentTokenCount) is a SUBSET of `input`
      (promptTokenCount), not a separate bucket. Adding it inflates by
      1,221,557,506 — 83%. It is moved out of input instead, keeping the total
      right and the cache split visible.
    - `total` (totalTokenCount) already equals input + output + thoughts + tool.
      Summing it alongside its own components is exactly 2x.

    Sessions must be grouped by the `sessionId` field, NOT per file: one session
    is checkpointed across up to 12 files, and 92 files here hold 52 sessions.
    Counting files as sessions would triple the session count and wreck every
    per-session duration.
    """
    if not base.is_dir():
        return []
    sessions = {}
    # Both extensions and any depth. The first version required exactly
    # <hash>/chats/session-*.json, so on a machine where Gemini writes .jsonl it
    # found ~/.gemini/tmp, read nothing, and was indistinguishable from Gemini
    # never having been used. A reader should be picky about what a token IS,
    # not about where the file sits.
    files = sorted(set(base.rglob("session-*.json")) | set(base.rglob("session-*.jsonl"))
                   | set(base.rglob("chats/*.json")) | set(base.rglob("chats/*.jsonl")))
    for f in files:
        for d in _gemini_docs(f):
            sid = d.get("sessionId") or f.stem
            rec = sessions.get(sid)
            if rec is None:
                rec = sessions[sid] = {
                    "cli": "gemini", "session_id": sid, "account": "gemini (local)",
                    "project": d.get("projectHash") or "-", "start": None, "end": None,
                    "turns": 0, "tokens": blank(), "_models": defaultdict(int),
                    "_stamps": []}
            for m in d.get("messages") or []:
                ts = m.get("timestamp")
                if ts:
                    rec["_stamps"].append(ts)
                    if rec["start"] is None or ts < rec["start"]:
                        rec["start"] = ts
                    if rec["end"] is None or ts > rec["end"]:
                        rec["end"] = ts
                t = m.get("tokens")
                if not isinstance(t, dict):
                    continue
                rec["turns"] += 1
                if m.get("model"):
                    rec["_models"][m["model"]] += 1
                inp = t.get("input", 0) or 0
                cached = t.get("cached", 0) or 0
                rec["tokens"]["input_tokens"] += max(0, inp - cached) + (t.get("tool", 0) or 0)
                rec["tokens"]["cache_read_input_tokens"] += min(cached, inp)
                # Thinking tokens are generated and billed as output.
                rec["tokens"]["output_tokens"] += (t.get("output", 0) or 0) + (t.get("thoughts", 0) or 0)
    return [finish(r) for r in sessions.values() if r["turns"]]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# kilo code — VS Code extension, one task dir per conversation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def vscode_roots(home):
    """Where the VS Code family stores user data, per platform.

    Linux keeps it in ~/.config/Code, macOS in ~/Library/Application Support/Code
    and Windows in %APPDATA%\\Code. The first version of this file hardcoded the
    Linux path, so on the MacBook and on Windows every VS Code-hosted agent read
    as "not installed" — a false negative that looks exactly like a tool nobody
    uses. Returns (label, path) for each channel that exists.
    """
    import os
    # stores.vscode_bases() is the one definition. This function had its own
    # copy of the platform branch while eight store paths hardcoded `.config`,
    # so the counter and the archiver disagreed on macOS by construction.
    bases = [home / b for b in stores.vscode_bases()]
    if os.name == "nt":
        # %APPDATA% wins where it is set to something other than the default,
        # which is the one case the relative form in stores.py cannot express.
        env = os.environ.get("APPDATA")
        if env:
            bases.insert(0, pathlib.Path(env))
    out = []
    for b in bases:
        for name in ("Code", "Code - Insiders", "VSCodium", "Code - OSS"):
            d = b / name
            if d.is_dir():
                out.append((name, d))
    return out


def vscode_state(home):
    """Every VS Code global state store, across channels and platforms.

    Yields (channel, path-to-state.vscdb). Insiders keeps a separate one, and a
    tool used in both has two independent histories — reading only the stable
    channel loses whichever half lives in the other.
    """
    for name, base in vscode_roots(home):
        db = base / "User" / "globalStorage" / "state.vscdb"
        if db.is_file():
            yield name, db


def first_last_seen(home, sessions):
    """When each tool was first and last used — including where no tokens survive.

    Two independent sources, and the second is the point:

      transcripts   the sessions this scan found. Precise, but only as old as
                    whatever has not been deleted.
      editor state  VS Code's own record. `survey.usage.firstActive` is a
                    first-use date, and per-model `lastUsed` a last-use one.
                    Neither carries tokens — which is exactly why they survive
                    when the transcripts do not.

    So a tool can report a first-seen date years before its oldest surviving
    session, and that gap is real information: it is the span the token counts
    cannot speak for. The source is recorded per date so the two are never
    confused for each other.
    """
    import sqlite3
    out = {}

    def note(cli, when, src):
        if not when:
            return
        e = out.setdefault(cli, {"first": None, "last": None, "sources": []})
        if e["first"] is None or when < e["first"]:
            e["first"] = when
        if e["last"] is None or when > e["last"]:
            e["last"] = when
        if src not in e["sources"]:
            e["sources"].append(src)

    for s in sessions:
        note(s.get("cli"), s.get("start"), "transcripts")
        note(s.get("cli"), s.get("end"), "transcripts")

    def iso(ms):
        try:
            return datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(
                ms / 1000, datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
        except Exception:
            return None

    for channel, db in vscode_state(home):
        try:
            con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db}?mode=ro", uri=True)
            rows = dict(con.execute("SELECT key, value FROM ItemTable"))
            con.close()
        except Exception:
            continue
        src = f"vscode:{channel}"

        for key, val in rows.items():
            if not isinstance(val, str):
                continue
            try:
                o = json.loads(val)
            except Exception:
                continue
            if key == "GitHub.copilot-chat" and isinstance(o, dict):
                u = (o.get("survey") or {}).get("usage") or {}
                note("copilot", iso(u.get("firstActive")), src)
                for d in (u.get("activeDays") or []):
                    note("copilot", iso(d), src)
            elif key.endswith("-usages") and isinstance(o, list):
                for item in o:
                    if isinstance(item, dict):
                        note("copilot", iso(item.get("lastUsed")), src)
            elif key == "kilocode.kilo-code" and isinstance(o, dict):
                for t in (o.get("taskHistory") or []):
                    note("kilocode", iso(t.get("ts")), src)
    return out


def read_kilocode(home, base=None):
    """Kilo Code (kilocode.kilo-code), a VS Code extension that bills per request.

    Worth reading for two reasons: it is real spend the account totals never saw,
    and because one of its requests called a Grok model, which is the clearest
    illustration of why cli and provider are separate fields: that request is
    Kilo Code spend and xAI service. Kilo Code is not Grok, and neither is
    xAI's own Grok CLI, which has its own reader below.

    Scans every VS Code channel — `Code`, `Code - Insiders`, VSCodium, and the
    OSS build. Checking only ~/.config/Code missed the Insiders profile, which is
    where the Grok usage was.

    Traps:
    - `tokensIn` ALREADY INCLUDES cacheReads and cacheWrites. The extension's own
      cost function computes uncached = tokensIn - cacheReads - cacheWrites, so
      adding them on top inflates by 64% here. Split, don't add.
    - state.vscdb's taskHistory[] is an end-of-task ROLLUP that restates these
      same per-request rows exactly. Read one or the other, never both. This
      reader takes the per-request records and ignores the rollup.

    `base` points the reader straight at a `tasks/` directory that lives
    somewhere other than a VS Code profile — the corpus keeps this store as
    `tools/kilocode/`. Without it this was the one reader that could only ever
    read the live tree, so the corpus could not be recounted for it.
    """
    if base is not None:
        return _kilocode_tasks(pathlib.Path(base), "corpus")
    out = []
    for label, root in vscode_roots(home):
        tasks = root / "User/globalStorage/kilocode.kilo-code/tasks"
        out.extend(_kilocode_tasks(tasks, label))
    return out


def _kilocode_tasks(tasks, label):
    """Every Kilo task under one `tasks/` directory, wherever that directory is."""
    out = []
    if tasks.is_dir():
        for tdir in sorted(p for p in tasks.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
            f = tdir / "ui_messages.json"
            if not f.is_file():
                continue
            try:
                msgs = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"))
            except Exception:
                continue
            rec = {"cli": "kilocode", "session_id": tdir.name,
                   "account": f"kilocode ({label})", "project": "-",
                   "start": None, "end": None, "turns": 0, "tokens": blank(),
                   "_models": defaultdict(int), "_stamps": []}
            provider = None
            for m in msgs if isinstance(msgs, list) else []:
                ts = m.get("ts")
                if isinstance(ts, (int, float)):
                    iso = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(
                        ts / 1000, datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
                    rec["_stamps"].append(iso)
                    if rec["start"] is None or iso < rec["start"]:
                        rec["start"] = iso
                    if rec["end"] is None or iso > rec["end"]:
                        rec["end"] = iso
                if m.get("say") != "api_req_started":
                    continue
                try:
                    p = json.loads(m.get("text") or "{}")
                except Exception:
                    continue
                tin = p.get("tokensIn") or 0
                if not tin and not (p.get("tokensOut") or 0):
                    continue              # aborted/streaming-start placeholder row
                cr, cw = p.get("cacheReads") or 0, p.get("cacheWrites") or 0
                rec["turns"] += 1
                rec["tokens"]["input_tokens"] += max(0, tin - cr - cw)
                rec["tokens"]["cache_read_input_tokens"] += cr
                rec["tokens"]["cache_creation_input_tokens"] += cw
                rec["tokens"]["output_tokens"] += p.get("tokensOut") or 0
                provider = p.get("inferenceProvider") or provider
            if not rec["turns"]:
                continue
            rec["_models"][_kilo_model(tdir, provider)] += 1
            out.append(finish(rec))
    return out


def _kilo_model(tdir, provider):
    """Model name for a Kilo task — it lives in the sibling conversation file."""
    f = tdir / "api_conversation_history.json"
    if f.is_file():
        try:
            m = re.search(r"<model>([^<]+)</model>",
                          f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")[:400000])
            if m:
                return m.group(1).split("/")[-1]
        except Exception:
            pass
    return provider or "unknown"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# grok — xAI official "Grok Build" CLI
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

@multi_base(".lmstudio/conversations")
def read_lmstudio(home, base):
    """LM Studio conversations — models that ran on this machine.

    Real tokens with no invoice behind them. Counted like any others and marked
    `billed: False`, because a token is a token regardless of who pays: the
    payer is a separate dimension, not a reason to leave work out of a total.

    Per-step counts live at
    messages[].versions[].steps[].genInfo.stats.{promptTokensCount,
    predictedTokensCount}, with the model in the sibling
    genInfo.indexedModelIdentifier — a real field, not a name scraped out of
    surrounding text.

    Two fields that must not be summed:
      genInfo.stats.totalTokensCount   a rollup of the two above (56/56 rows)
      conversation-level tokenCount    context bookkeeping. It sums to 4,329
                                       against 119,774 in the per-step records,
                                       a 27.7x shortfall that proves it is a
                                       context size and not a running total.

    Ollama is installed and deliberately absent here: ~/.ollama holds three
    files — two SSH keys and a shell history — and nothing anywhere records
    prompt_eval_count or eval_count. Its models live on an external drive via
    OLLAMA_MODELS. Verified rather than assumed, so the zero is a measurement.
    """
    if not base.is_dir():
        return []
    out = []
    for f in sorted(base.glob("*.json")):
        try:
            o = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"))
        except Exception:
            continue
        rec = {"cli": "lmstudio", "session_id": f.stem.split(".")[0],
               "account": "lmstudio (local)", "project": "-",
               "start": None, "end": None, "turns": 0, "tokens": blank(),
               "_models": defaultdict(int), "_stamps": []}
        try:
            ms = int(f.stem.split(".")[0])
            rec["start"] = rec["end"] = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(
                ms / 1000, datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
        except Exception:
            pass
        for m in o.get("messages") or []:
            for v in m.get("versions") or []:
                for st in v.get("steps") or []:
                    g = (st.get("genInfo") or {})
                    stats = g.get("stats") or {}
                    pin = stats.get("promptTokensCount") or 0
                    pout = stats.get("predictedTokensCount") or 0
                    if not (pin or pout):
                        continue
                    rec["turns"] += 1
                    rec["tokens"]["input_tokens"] += pin
                    rec["tokens"]["output_tokens"] += pout
                    mid = g.get("indexedModelIdentifier")
                    if mid:
                        rec["_models"][mid.split("/")[-1]] += 1
        if rec["turns"]:
            out.append(finish(rec))
    return out


@multi_base(".grok/sessions", ".grok/archived_sessions")
def read_grok(home, base):
    """xAI Grok CLI sessions.

    Not installed on this machine, so this reader returns nothing here — it is
    written for the other machines in the fleet. Two different tools share the
    name and only one records usage: @vibe-kit/grok-cli (community npm package)
    stores none, while xAI's official Grok Build CLI writes JSON-RPC session
    updates to ~/.grok/{sessions,archived_sessions}/<url-encoded-cwd>/<id>/.

    Traps, from the published record format:
    - Only `turn_completed` updates are end-of-turn totals. `usage_snapshot` is
      a mid-turn snapshot carrying the SAME field names; counting both
      double-counts every turn.
    - usage.inputTokens/outputTokens is the SUM over usage.modelUsage.<model>.*.
      Take the per-model breakdown when present, the top level only as fallback.
    - cachedReadTokens is a subset of inputTokens and reasoningTokens a subset of
      outputTokens, matching xAI's OpenAI-compatible convention.
    - params._meta.totalTokens is a running CONTEXT counter, not billed usage.
    """
    out = []
    for sdir in sorted(p for p in base.glob("*/*") if p.is_dir()):
        f = sdir / "updates.jsonl"
        if not f.is_file():
            continue
        rec = {"cli": "grok", "session_id": sdir.name, "account": "grok (local)",
               "project": urllib.parse.unquote(sdir.parent.name), "start": None,
               "end": None, "turns": 0, "tokens": blank(),
               "_models": defaultdict(int), "_stamps": []}
        for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"):
            try:
                o = json.loads(line)
            except Exception:
                continue
            ts = o.get("timestamp")
            if isinstance(ts, (int, float)):
                ts = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(
                    ts if ts < 1e11 else ts / 1000,
                    datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
            if isinstance(ts, str) and ts:
                rec["_stamps"].append(ts)
                if rec["start"] is None or ts < rec["start"]:
                    rec["start"] = ts
                if rec["end"] is None or ts > rec["end"]:
                    rec["end"] = ts
            upd = ((o.get("params") or {}).get("update")) or {}
            if upd.get("sessionUpdate") != "turn_completed":
                continue              # usage_snapshot would double-count
            usage = upd.get("usage") or {}
            per_model = usage.get("modelUsage") or {}
            rows = list(per_model.items()) or [("grok", usage)]
            rec["turns"] += 1
            for model, u in rows:
                if not isinstance(u, dict):
                    continue
                rec["_models"][model] += 1
                inp = u.get("inputTokens", 0) or 0
                cached = u.get("cachedReadTokens", 0) or 0
                rec["tokens"]["input_tokens"] += max(0, inp - cached)
                rec["tokens"]["cache_read_input_tokens"] += min(cached, inp)
                rec["tokens"]["output_tokens"] += u.get("outputTokens", 0) or 0
        if rec["turns"]:
            out.append(finish(rec))
    return out


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# antigravity — protobuf inside SQLite, plus AES-256-GCM encrypted .pb
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Google's Antigravity CLI stores usage as unnamed protobuf fields, and puts the
# two largest conversations in encrypted files. The key below is a string
# constant compiled into the `agy` binary (found at file offset 0x4ab02c9,
# alongside the symbols proto_saver.WithEncryptionKey and hasEncryption), so
# there is no secret being exfiltrated here — it is the same fixed key shipped
# to every user, which is why the files can be read at all.
AGY_KEY = b"safeCodeiumworldKeYsecretBalloon"

# Field numbers inside the ModelUsageStats submessage (field 9 of a step's
# metadata). Names come from the FileDescriptorProtos embedded in the binary.
AGY_UNCACHED, AGY_OUTPUT, AGY_CACHED = 2, 3, 5
AGY_OUT_PART_A, AGY_OUT_PART_B, AGY_REQUEST_ID = 9, 10, 11


def _pb_varint(b, i):
    r = s = 0
    while True:
        if i >= len(b):
            raise ValueError
        c = b[i]
        i += 1
        r |= (c & 0x7F) << s
        s += 7
        if not c & 0x80:
            return r, i
        if s > 70:
            raise ValueError


def _pb_fields(b):
    """Parse one protobuf message level, or None if it is not one.

    Requires the parse to consume the buffer EXACTLY. Without that, arbitrary
    binary decodes as a plausible-looking message and yields enormous fake
    "token counts" — a first attempt at this reported 1.49e21 tokens.
    """
    d, i = {}, 0
    while i < len(b):
        try:
            tag, i = _pb_varint(b, i)
        except ValueError:
            return None
        fn, wt = tag >> 3, tag & 7
        if fn == 0 or fn > 536870911:
            return None
        try:
            if wt == 0:
                v, i = _pb_varint(b, i)
            elif wt == 1:
                v, i = b[i:i + 8], i + 8
            elif wt == 2:
                ln, i = _pb_varint(b, i)
                if i + ln > len(b):
                    return None
                v, i = b[i:i + ln], i + ln
            elif wt == 5:
                v, i = b[i:i + 4], i + 4
            else:
                return None
        except (ValueError, IndexError):
            return None
        d.setdefault(fn, []).append(v)
    return d if i == len(b) else None


def _agy_usage(blob, out, depth=0):
    """Collect every ModelUsageStats found anywhere inside a step's metadata."""
    if depth > 14:
        return out
    d = _pb_fields(blob)
    if not d:
        return out
    for fn, vals in d.items():
        for v in vals:
            if not isinstance(v, bytes) or len(v) < 2:
                continue
            inner = _pb_fields(v)
            if not inner:
                continue
            if fn == 9:
                def g(k, _f=inner):
                    v = _f.get(k, [0])[0]
                    return v if isinstance(v, int) else 0
                unc, o, cac = g(AGY_UNCACHED), g(AGY_OUTPUT), g(AGY_CACHED)
                a, bb = g(AGY_OUT_PART_A), g(AGY_OUT_PART_B)
                # Structural signature of a real usage record: the output total
                # equals its two components. Everything else at field 9 is a
                # coincidental match, and this is what separates them.
                if (unc or o or cac) and a + bb == o and max(unc, o, cac) < 50_000_000:
                    rid = inner.get(AGY_REQUEST_ID, [None])[0]
                    key = rid if isinstance(rid, bytes) else (unc, o, cac, a, bb)
                    out[key] = (unc, o, cac)
                    continue
            _agy_usage(v, out, depth + 1)
    return out


def _agy_times(blob, out, depth=0):
    """Every google.protobuf.Timestamp nested anywhere inside a trajectory.

    A Timestamp is {1: seconds} with an optional {2: nanos} and nothing else,
    so it is identifiable by shape without the .proto. Three guards keep this
    from collecting coincidence: the message must contain only fields 1 and 2,
    be at most 12 bytes, and hold a plausible epoch second.

    Walking nested rather than reading the top level matters for the encrypted
    .pb files: those are a whole trajectory in one blob, so the top level has a
    single time and every per-step time is buried. Those two files hold 88% of
    Antigravity's tokens here, and both reported a duration of 0 without this.
    On the SQLite conversations, where the top-level read already worked, this
    is a strict superset — verified per conversation, none lost time.
    """
    if depth > 12:
        return out
    d = _pb_fields(blob)
    if not d:
        return out
    for vals in d.values():
        for v in vals:
            if not isinstance(v, bytes) or len(v) < 2:
                continue
            inner = _pb_fields(v)
            if not inner:
                continue
            sec = inner.get(1, [None])[0]
            if (isinstance(sec, int) and 1_500_000_000 < sec < 2_500_000_000
                    and len(v) <= 12 and set(inner).issubset({1, 2})):
                out.append(sec)
            else:
                _agy_times(v, out, depth + 1)
    return out


def _agy_decrypt(raw):
    """AES-256-GCM with a 12-byte nonce prefix, or None if it cannot be read."""
    try:
        from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM
    except ImportError:
        return None
    try:
        return AESGCM(AGY_KEY).decrypt(raw[:12], raw[12:], None)
    except Exception:
        return None


# A model id as Antigravity writes it, which is NOT the public Gemini naming:
# gemini-3.6-flash-high, gemini-3-flash-a, gemini_coder, gemini-3.5-flash-low.
# Underscores and letter suffixes are normal, so a pattern demanding a digit
# straight after the dash misses most of them.
AGY_MODEL = re.compile(rb"gemini[-_][0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._\-]{0,26}")
# Rejected because they match that shape and are not models: filenames, and the
# gemini-cli-* extension packages.
AGY_NOT_MODEL = re.compile(rb"\.(json|md|zip|txt|py|js)$|^gemini-cli")


def _agy_model(con):
    """The model for a conversation, from gen_metadata where it is recorded.

    Read from the field that holds it rather than by scanning the whole
    conversation. Scanning finds `used_claude_conservative` (a feature flag) and
    `claude-alt.md` (one of the user's own filenames) and reports Antigravity as
    having run Claude models, which it did not — every conversation on this
    machine resolves to Gemini. Substring matches are not model attribution.
    """
    try:
        rows = [bytes(r[0]) for r in con.execute("select data from gen_metadata") if r[0]]
    except Exception:
        return None
    best = defaultdict(int)
    for b in rows:
        for m in AGY_MODEL.findall(b):
            if AGY_NOT_MODEL.search(m):
                continue
            best[m.decode("ascii", "ignore").rstrip("-._")] += 1
    if not best:
        return None
    # Prefer the most specific id: the longest one, which carries the tier
    # suffix (gemini-3.6-flash-high over gemini-3.6-flash).
    return max(best, key=lambda k: (len(k), best[k]))


@multi_base(".gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations")
def read_antigravity(home, base):
    """Google Antigravity CLI conversations.

    Two storage forms, both counted:

      conversations/<uuid>.db   SQLite; usage is a protobuf BLOB in steps.metadata
      conversations/<uuid>.pb   the same protobuf, AES-256-GCM encrypted

    Traps, every one of them a duplicate of the authoritative record rather than
    new usage. Reading all of them sums to exactly 4.00x the truth:

      steps.step_payload 5.9.*      == steps.metadata 9.* (embedded copy)
      steps.metadata 28.2.*         == steps.metadata 9.* (in-blob mirror)
      gen_metadata.data 1.4.*       a strict SUBSET of steps.metadata 9.*
      gen_metadata.data 1.17.2.*    byte-identical mirror of 1.4.*
      fields 9 and 10               components of field 3, not additions

    Only steps.metadata field 9 is read, deduplicated on the per-request server
    id in field 11, because the same request appears in several steps.

    This depends on an undocumented key and unnamed field numbers, so it is the
    one reader here that a vendor update can silently break. It fails soft: a
    conversation it cannot parse contributes nothing and is reported, rather
    than being counted as zero.
    """
    if not base.is_dir():
        return []
    import sqlite3
    out, unreadable = [], 0
    for f in sorted(list(base.glob("*.db")) + list(base.glob("*.pb"))):
        usage, stamps, secs, models = {}, [], [], defaultdict(int)
        if f.suffix == ".db":
            try:
                con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{f}?mode=ro", uri=True)
                rows = con.execute("select metadata from steps").fetchall()
                named = _agy_model(con)
                con.close()
            except Exception:
                unreadable += 1
                continue
            blobs = [r[0] for r in rows if isinstance(r[0], (bytes, bytearray))]
            if named:
                models[named] += 1000        # authoritative: outvotes any scan
        else:
            plain = _agy_decrypt(f.read_bytes())
            if plain is None:
                unreadable += 1
                continue
            blobs = [plain]
        for b in blobs:
            b = bytes(b)
            _agy_usage(b, usage)
            # Fallback for the encrypted .pb files, which have no gen_metadata
            # table to read. Same pattern, same exclusions.
            for m in AGY_MODEL.findall(b):
                if not AGY_NOT_MODEL.search(m):
                    models[m.decode("ascii", "ignore").rstrip("-._")] += 1
            _agy_times(b, secs)
        stamps = [datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(x, datetime.timezone.utc)
                  .isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z") for x in sorted(set(secs))]
        if not usage:
            continue
        unc = sum(v[0] for v in usage.values())
        o = sum(v[1] for v in usage.values())
        cac = sum(v[2] for v in usage.values())
        rec = {"cli": "antigravity", "session_id": f.stem,
               "account": "antigravity (local)", "project": "-",
               "start": None, "end": None, "turns": len(usage),
               "tokens": blank(), "_models": models or {"antigravity": 1},
               "_stamps": stamps}
        rec["tokens"]["input_tokens"] = unc
        rec["tokens"]["cache_read_input_tokens"] = cac
        rec["tokens"]["output_tokens"] = o
        if stamps:
            rec["start"], rec["end"] = min(stamps), max(stamps)
        else:
            # No decodable step times. Fall back to the file's mtime for WHEN,
            # but leave start == end so active_minutes reports 0 rather than
            # inventing a span. The earlier version did this for every
            # conversation, which gave all 19 a duration of exactly 0 — that
            # reads as "no time spent" instead of "not measured".
            try:
                ts = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(
                    f.stat().st_mtime, datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
                rec["start"] = rec["end"] = ts
            except Exception:
                pass
        out.append(finish(rec))
    if unreadable:
        sys.stderr.write(f"  antigravity: {unreadable} conversation(s) unreadable "
                         f"(install `cryptography` to read encrypted .pb)\n")
    return out

# count it" and "there is nothing to count", and those are opposite facts.
